Anthropic S-1 TPU Trainium cost per token efficiency inference cost decline

sources_considered.why: Covers DeepSeek V4 price pressure and a later planned price hike. These are price signals, not cost evidence.
Shows Anthropic runs a mix of chips without saying how much runs on each, so cost changes cannot be pinned to one chip.
Vendor-blog estimates based on AWS's own throughput claims. Not independent.

receipt.public_excerpt: Chinese AI companies are responding with steep API discounts and new billing experiments

evidence_items.explanation: DeepSeek V4 set off price cuts. Prices are not costs, and the same outlet later reported a planned DeepSeek price hike, so this does not show AI became cheaper to provide.

receipt.public_excerpt: Anthropic runs a “multi-chip compute architecture across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, Nvidia GPUs, and AMD GPUs,” without giving any percentage splits

evidence_items.explanation: A major lab using TPUs and Trainium does not split its compute by chip, so any cost changes cannot be attributed to the named chips.

unresolved_gaps: I found no filing or independent measurement that attributes a lasting fall in overall LLM serving cost to any named chip or to DeepSeek.
